why: The statement asks whether every point (ε, 1/2+ε) is an exponent pair. The only event that adds exponent pairs (Tao–Trudgian–Yang, January 2025) exhibits four explicit pairs with ℓ−k between about 0.71 and 0.86, far from the conjectured family where ℓ−k = 1/2. They are new members of the known set, but they neither settle any point of the family nor bound a quantity the statement names, so the scope is none and not bound. The close call was the competing reading that improved β bounds in Table 1 move the conjecture's quantity. The record never shows any β value reaching α/2, and the statement is about the specific family, not the β-function, so I did not count it. The zeta-bound papers (Bourgain, Guth–Maynard, Revers) concern neighbouring questions, so they are variant. Trudgian–Yang 2023, Elaissaoui and Li bound or settle nothing here, so they are none. No AI system is credited in any event. The Alpöge–Furman Claude result concerns another problem and is correctly not an event here.
doubts: Table 1 of arXiv:2501.16779 was not read. If its β improvements were read as moving the conjecture's own quantity, the ANTEDB event could arguably be a bound. Bourgain's 2017 JAMS publication and Guth–Maynard's Annals publication rest on search listings that were not opened.
